[=SPO Architecture Map=]

This folder is secondary documentation. It is laid out in the same order you usually need when reading the repository:

o 1. repo shape and entry points
o 2. surface language
o 3. lowering and backend boundary
o 4. VM and module loading
o 5. tests, limits, and next work

Primary sources still remain:

- [<../SPO_CS/src/|SPO_CS/src/>]
- [<../SPO_CS/Modules/|SPO_CS/Modules/>]
- [<../SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/|SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/>]
- [<../SPO_CS/SPO_CS.csproj|SPO_CS/SPO_CS.csproj>]

Complementary review documents live in [<../AI-Review/README.md|AI-Review/>].

Treat this folder as a reading aid, not as the authority. When a claim matters, confirm it against the source tree and the test host.

[=How To Use This Folder Safely=]

- Start here for code-map and pipeline orientation, not for final debugging decisions.
- Use [<../AI-Review/README.md|AI-Review/>] for prioritized findings and active breakage.
- When a statement affects implementation work, re-check it against source and one of the verification commands below before repeating it elsewhere.
- When you update this folder, update the affected evidence in the same pass: source anchors, commands, and current observed behavior.

Path convention for this folder:

- bare prose paths like [.txt|src/.], [.txt|Modules/.], and [.txt|Regression.Tests/.] refer to [.txt|SPO_CS/src/.], [.txt|SPO_CS/Modules/.], and [.txt|SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/.]
- runnable commands below assume the current working directory is [.txt|SPO_CS/.] because [.txt|mRegression_Tests.] resolves [.txt|Regression.Tests/.] through [.txt|mFS.CWD().]
- from the repo root next to [.txt|AI-Doc/.], use [.txt|Push-Location .\SPO_CS.] first

If you inspect these files from Windows PowerShell, prefer [.txt|Get-Content -Encoding UTF8.] so [.txt|§.] and [.txt|€.] render correctly.

This index was checked on [.txt|2026-04-22.] against the current source tree and these test commands:

[.powershell
|Push-Location .\SPO_CS
|dotnet run --project .\SPO_CS.csproj -- --list --plainText
|dotnet run --project .\SPO_CS.csproj -- --plainText --stopOnFirstFail --matchAny mModule_Tests
|dotnet run --project .\SPO_CS.csproj -- --plainText --showPassedGroups --showPassedTests --stopOnFirstFail --matchAny 07_12_GenericTypes
|Pop-Location
.]

Run those checks sequentially. Parallel [.txt|dotnet run.] invocations against the same project can lock [.txt|bin/Debug/net10.0/SPO_CS.exe.] or [.txt|obj/Debug/net10.0/SPO_CS.dll.]. After one successful build, the targeted checks above can be repeated with [.txt|--no-build.].

Operational caveat:

- keep [.txt|--matchAny.] and [.txt|--matchAll.] last; [.txt|mRunTests.cs.] treats every remaining argument as filter text
- running from the repo root without changing into [.txt|SPO_CS/.] currently prints [.txt|Folder not found: mFS+tFolder.] and silently drops the regression suite from discovery

Current verified state:

- full suite from [.txt|SPO_CS/.]: [.txt|393.] leaf checks, [.txt|1.] failing leaf check ([.txt|mModule_Tests -> Maybe.])
- repo-root run via [.txt|dotnet run --project .\SPO_CS\SPO_CS.csproj -- --plainText.]: [.txt|246.] leaf checks, [.txt|1.] failing leaf check, plus [.txt|Folder not found: mFS+tFolder.]
- the full test tree lists successfully when launched from [.txt|SPO_CS/.]
- [.txt|Std.], [.txt|Char.], and [.txt|Text.] pass [.txt|mModule_Tests.]
- [.txt|Maybe.] still fails reproducibly with [.txt|expected generic type but '_tMaybe...'.]
- regression [.txt|07_12_GenericTypes.] still passes all three regression checks
- [.txt|.SPO.] modules are compared against sibling [.txt|.ILT.] artifacts and write [.txt|.ILT.new.] on drift
- the current [.txt|Maybe.] failure is reached before VM execution:
  [.txt|mModule.Init(...).] first calls [.txt|mSPO_Parser.Module.ParseText(...).ToILT().], where [.txt|ToILT().] is the parsed-module extension currently defined in [.txt|mSPO_Interpreter.], and the failing source location is [.txt|SPO_CS/Modules/Maybe.SPO.] line 7 at [.txt|.tMaybe tIn.]

[=Highest-Priority Breakage=]

The most important current limitation is not "generics are broken" in general, but a narrower module-compilation boundary:

- regression [.txt|07_12_GenericTypes.] proves that generic syntax, lowering, and IL execution still work for at least one end-to-end path
- [.txt|mModule_Tests.Maybe.] fails earlier, while compiling [.txt|Modules/Maybe.SPO.] through [.txt|mSPO_Parser.Module.ParseText(...).ToILT().] and [.txt|mSPO_AST_Types.]
- the concrete failing expression is [.txt|.tMaybe tIn.] in [<../SPO_CS/Modules/Maybe.SPO|SPO_CS/Modules/Maybe.SPO>]
- the concrete failure site in code is the generic-application case in [<../SPO_CS/src/mSPO_AST_Types.cs|SPO_CS/src/mSPO_AST_Types.cs>], which rejects the head type with [.txt|expected generic type but '_tMaybe...'.]

Why this matters for triage:

- do not start by changing [.txt|mVM.], [.txt|mVM_Data.], or [.txt|mIL_GenerateOpcodes.] for this failure
- first inspect module-source type analysis and type-constructor resolution in [.txt|mSPO_AST_Types.], plus the parsed-module [.txt|.ToILT().] helper in [<../SPO_CS/src/mSPO_Interpreter.cs|SPO_CS/src/mSPO_Interpreter.cs>] and the [.txt|.SPO -> .ILT.] verification path in [<../SPO_CS/src/mModule.cs|SPO_CS/src/mModule.cs>]
- only if the failure moves past type analysis should the runtime documents in [.txt|30_runtime/.] become the next debugging layer

[=High-Value Source Anchors=]

When this folder and the code disagree, re-check these files first:

- [<../SPO_CS/src/mSPO_Interpreter.cs|SPO_CS/src/mSPO_Interpreter.cs>]
  full SPO pipeline entry point, parsed-module [.txt|ToILT().] helper, initial scope seeding, and final error shaping
- [<../SPO_CS/src/mModule.cs|SPO_CS/src/mModule.cs>]
  module dependency injection, [.txt|.SPO.] vs [.txt|.ILT.] loading, and [.txt|.ILT.] drift checks
- [<../SPO_CS/src/mIL_GenerateOpcodes.cs|SPO_CS/src/mIL_GenerateOpcodes.cs>]
  the actual boundary where IL becomes VM opcodes and runtime type operations
- [<../SPO_CS/src/mVM.cs|SPO_CS/src/mVM.cs>]
  fixed registers, opcode execution, and the real runtime support surface
- [<../SPO_CS/src/mRunTests.cs|SPO_CS/src/mRunTests.cs>]
  authoritative CLI flag behavior for listing, filtering, and printing tests
- [<../SPO_CS/src/mRegression.Tests.cs|SPO_CS/src/mRegression.Tests.cs>] and [<../SPO_CS/src/mModule.Tests.cs|SPO_CS/src/mModule.Tests.cs>]
  the executable contracts this folder claims to summarize

[=Refreshing This Folder=]

When parser, lowering, type, VM, or module code changes, update this folder in this order:

o 1. Re-run the checks listed above.
o 2. Re-open the source anchors for the area you changed.
o 3. For type-runtime changes, inspect all three layers before editing docs:
   [.txt|mVM_Data.tOpCode.], [.txt|mIL_GenerateOpcodes.GenerateOpcodes(...).], and [.txt|mVM.Step(...).].
o 4. Only then update the affected [.txt|AI-Doc.] file, keeping verified behavior and unimplemented behavior clearly separated.

[=Architecture Invariants=]

- [.txt|SPO_CS/SPO_CS.csproj.] builds one [.txt|net10.0.] executable that contains production code and tests together.
- [.txt|.SPO.] and [.txt|.ILT.] meet architecturally in [.txt|mIL_AST.tModule.].
- [.txt|mTokenizer.] is shared by both frontends.
- [.txt|mVM_Type.] is shared by parsing, type analysis, lowering, opcode generation, and the VM.
- a SPO module is internally turned into an initialization lambda:
  [.txt|ImportPattern => { Commands; RETURN Export }.]
- [.txt|mModule.] is both module loader and canonical [.txt|.ILT.] verification step

[=Corrections Pulled Toward the Code=]

- SPO surface syntax and IL text syntax are intentionally not identical.
  Generic, interface, and recursive type keywords differ across that boundary.
- generics are not globally broken:
  regression [.txt|07_12_GenericTypes.] passes end-to-end, while [.txt|mModule_Tests.Maybe.] still fails across the module boundary
- the type system is ahead of runtime type evaluation:
  [.txt|mVM_Data.] and [.txt|mIL_GenerateOpcodes.] know more [.txt|Type*.] cases than [.txt|mVM.Step(...).] currently executes
